name_en: Gunma konnyaku-imo — the konjac corm behind most of Japan's konnyaku, grown on volcanic slopes
summary_ja: 赤城山や榛名山の裾野の畑で育てられるこんにゃくの球茎。国内の生産量の大部分を群馬県が占めるとされ、生のままでは強いえぐみがあって食べられず、粉にして石灰で固めるとこんにゃくになる。収穫まで2〜3年かける手間のかかる作物という。
summary_en: The corm of the konjac plant, grown in fields on the lower slopes of Mount Akagi and Mount Haruna. Gunma is said to produce most of Japan's crop. Inedible raw because of a harsh, stinging acridity, it is milled to flour and set with lime to become konnyaku. It takes two to three years of replanting to reach harvest size.

name_en: Chiba rakkasei — peanuts from the volcanic-soil fields of the Hokuso plateau
summary_ja: 千葉県北部の八街市を中心とした北総台地で育つ落花生。火山灰の軽い土が地中で実を太らせるのに合うとされ、国内の生産量の大部分を千葉が占めるという。収穫後に畑で株を積み上げて乾かす「ぼっち」の姿が秋の風景になっている。
summary_en: Peanuts grown on the Hokuso plateau of northern Chiba, centered on Yachimata. The light volcanic soil is said to suit a plant that swells its pods underground, and Chiba accounts for most of Japan's crop. The stacks of harvested plants left to dry in the fields, called botchi, are part of the autumn landscape.
